title: Characterization of zero-error randomized computation
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model closed under racing two efficient Boolean verifiers, testing whether an efficient verifier returns a specified answer, and taking polynomially many independent verifier trials. For every language $L$ of bit strings, $L$ has an efficient polynomial-witness randomized verifier that never gives an incorrect answer and outputs no answer with probability at most $1/2$ if and only if both $L$ and its complement have efficient polynomial-witness randomized verifiers that accept members with probability at least $2/3$ and never accept nonmembers.
